item.title: Re: Fireproof Rescue Dog
item.content:encoded:
Hello BreakerBreaker! lets take a look :)

+ show block
– hide block

Concept:

This SCP is a former SAR (Search and Rescue) dog that is completely unaffected by fire and smoke. When irritated, the dog is also able to raise its internal body temperature to an unnaturally high level, allowing it to essentially burn those who come into contact with it. Visually, the dog is a completely average looking dalmatian. Given that it was an SAR animal, the dog had a handler. However, the handler was entirely non-anomalous and the dog’s anomalous protection did not extend to them nor anything other than itself.

Overall I think this is solid, my one concern here is its purpose. While it has a strong motive, there doesn't seem to be much of a reason for it exist in the first place, which (at least for me) takes some of my focus away from the narrative, as I'm continually asking myself "why".

- that said, this is a fairly minor issue, as the narrative isn't centred around that aspect.

Narrative:

The central narrative of this SCP Article would be the history of the SCP’s life prior to containment. This would be told through SAR incident reports recovered by the Foundation, detailing calls the dog was used on and how the dog and it’s handler performed. The reports would be written by the dog’s handler and would detail their specific experiences working with the dog during the incident.

I mainly second Cybersqyd here.

The dog is contained by the Foundation after it gives several children second and third degree burns. This result is from the dog spitting on and biting the children when they irritated it.

This incident is what alerts the Foundation to the dog’s existence. The dog is subsequently contained, with it’s handler and any witnesses to the incident anesthetized.

The article would end several years after the dog is contained, with a researcher in charge of the animal noting its declining health and mental state. The researcher makes a request to their superiors to suggest the dog be used for SAR work once again, this time for the Foundation. This portion of the article is told through an email.

Overall this sounds fairly solid too, my only real question; why didn't the Foundation see if they could utilise the dog earlier? considering they know about its history, and its general behaviour. It sounds like they would've at least tried at some points to use it for something. Rather than (assumably), continually keeping it locked away.- what was their reason for doing so?

A lot of the narrative will be dependant on how its executed, and the concept overall is workable. With that in mind, here is your second GreenLight..

Cheers,

RED

item.title: Re: Fireproof Rescue Dog
item.content:encoded:
hmm. I'm a little conflicted on this. There's definitely a solid emotional core to this, and I think the way you're wanting to tell it will be effective for that; but on some level it feels…a little expected maybe?

I have some concerns that the SAR incident reports will be hard to pull off well: it feels like they might struggle to keep a reader on board since they're effectively passive characterisation designed to make us care about the dog, without much like, narratively pulling our interest forward; and ensuring you have enough reports to get a reader to care without having so many that the reader gets bored will potentially be hard to balance.

This said: I think figuring out whether you've got the balance right is gonna be easiest at the drafting stage and so I'm gonna greenlight this. I'm also gonna suggest you check out Wilson's Wildlife Solutions since this kinda thing feels like it could really easily tie in there.
